sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Radha Mohan Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the third bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.992 of 2021 at Police Station-Khurja Nagar, District-Bulandshahar under Sections 420, 467,
468, 471, 34 IPC and Section 66D of the I.T. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 03.09.2021.
The first and second bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 31.03.202 and 09.11.2022 respectively.

The following arguments made by Shri Radha Mohan Pandey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
(1). The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial.
(2). The trial is moving at a snail's pace and and shows no sign of early conclusion.

Rizwan vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174434030/
1 (3).
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial.
(4). Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite incarceration of the applicant.
(5). The right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
(6). The status report sent by the learned trial court records that six witnesses have been examined while the prosecution proposes to examine 16 witnesses.
(7). The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Rizwan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
However, the learned trial court shall proceed with the trial expeditiously in adherence to the order dated 26.04.2023.

A copy of this order be communicated to the learned trial judge through the learned District Judge,
Bulandshahar by the Registrar (Compliance) by FAX.

Order Date :- 22.5.2023 Ashish Tripathi  Rizwan vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174434030/
